## Kyoto Trip Overview: 4 Days, 2 Adults, USD 1,800 Budget
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/map.svg

A comfortable Kyoto plan is very doable within your budget if you stay near a major transit hub and keep each day grouped by area.
Best fit: **Kyoto Station area** for the easiest overall commuting, or **Gion/Kawaramachi** if you want a more atmospheric stay with slightly better walking access.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Cost Plan
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar.svg

| Day | Focus | Highlights | Est. Transit for 2 | Est. Food for 2 | Est. Paid Entries for 2 | Day Total |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Mar 18 | Higashiyama + Gion | Kiyomizu-dera, Sannenzaka, Yasaka Shrine, Gion walk | USD 10–14 | USD 70–110 | USD 10–18 | USD 90–142 |
| Mar 19 | Arashiyama + Western Kyoto | Bamboo Grove, Tenryu-ji area, river walk, Okochi Sanso area | USD 12–18 | USD 75–120 | USD 20–40 | USD 107–178 |
| Mar 20 | Central Kyoto + Nishiki | Nijo Castle area, Nishiki Market, Teramachi/Shinkyogoku stroll, Pontocho evening | USD 8–12 | USD 80–130 | USD 15–30 | USD 103–172 |
| Mar 21 | Northern Kyoto + Philosopher’s Path | Ginkaku-ji area, Philosopher’s Path, Nanzen-ji vicinity, quiet café stop | USD 12–18 | USD 70–115 | USD 10–20 | USD 92–153 |

### March 18 — Higashiyama Temples, Old Streets, and Gion
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Start at **Kiyomizu-dera** early, then walk downhill through **Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka** before crowds build.
- Afternoon: Visit **Yasaka Shrine** and continue into **Maruyama Park** for a relaxed temple-and-garden pace.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f8/A199_Japan_Kyoto_Maruyama_Park_Gion_Ar%C3%A9a_%284764445344%29.jpg Alt=Afternoon: Visit **Yasaka Shrine** and continue into **Maruyama Park** for a relaxed temple-and-garden pace, Kyoto, Japan
- Evening: Do a low-key **Gion neighborhood walk** around Hanamikoji and Shirakawa; keep dinner in the area.
- Food: Try a Kyoto-style set meal or tofu lunch near Higashiyama, then a lighter kaiseki-style dinner if budget allows.
- Transit estimate: **USD 10–14** for buses/taxis/short rail hops for 2.

### March 19 — Arashiyama Nature, Temples, and Riverside Time
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Go to **Arashiyama Bamboo Grove** early, then continue to the **Tenryu-ji** area.
- Afternoon: Add a peaceful riverside walk and, if energy and budget allow, a paid garden stop such as **Okochi Sanso**.
- Evening: Return to central Kyoto for an easy dinner, or stay west for a quieter night.
- Food: Build around a soba or yudofu lunch in Arashiyama; dinner can be simple and still feel special.
- Transit estimate: **USD 12–18** for 2, depending on train/bus mix.

### March 20 — Central Kyoto Markets, Castle Area, and Evening Alleys
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- Morning: Visit **Nijo Castle area** or nearby historical streets for a less crowded cultural start.
- Afternoon: Spend time at **Nishiki Market** for tasting bites and casual shopping, then stroll **Teramachi/Shinkyogoku**.
- Evening: End with a calm **Pontocho lane walk** and dinner along the river-adjacent center.
- Food: This is your best day for snack-style grazing at Nishiki plus one sit-down dinner.
- Transit estimate: **USD 8–12** for 2.

### March 21 — Northern Kyoto, Quiet Paths, and a Gentle Finish
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Head to **Ginkaku-ji** area for a quieter temple start and soft morning light.
- Afternoon: Walk the **Philosopher’s Path** at an unhurried pace, then visit **Nanzen-ji vicinity** if you want one more temple stop.
- Evening: Keep the final night simple with a neighborhood dinner and an early return.
- Food: Choose a café lunch or noodle shop along the east side; save budget for a comfortable final dinner.
- Transit estimate: **USD 12–18** for 2.

## Best Hotel Area to Minimize Commuting
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

### Recommended: Kyoto Station Area
- Best for: easy airport/rail access, simple transfers, and flexible day trips.
- Why it works: it keeps you central for Arashiyama, Higashiyama, and northern Kyoto without overpaying for location.
- Good for budget control: you can usually find more hotel choices here than in Gion.

### Strong Alternative: Gion / Kawaramachi
- Best for: walking access to Higashiyama, Gion, Pontocho, and central dining.
- Trade-off: often a bit pricier, but you may save time and some local transit.
- Good if: you value atmosphere and evening strolls more than rail convenience.

## Budget Fit for 2 Adults

- Hotel: **USD 700–1,000** for 4 nights in a solid mid-range stay, depending on area and booking timing.
- Food: **USD 295–475** total for 4 days if you mix casual lunches with one nicer dinner daily.
- Local transit: **USD 42–62** total.
- Entries and small extras: **USD 55–108** total.
- Estimated total excluding flights: **USD 1,092–1,645**.

That leaves a comfortable buffer inside your **USD 1,800** cap for nicer meals, taxis, or a better hotel.
